what: the qualification run of ports/php/cheribsd: does the purecap interpreter start and run a script at all
pin: php 5.0.0, museum tarball sha256 5783e0c0ba94f165633a565fe73a83e59cf17b6880ef95fa8f936dc6301d6919, tree patches 0001 and 0002 (the same two the virtual port applies; 0003, the Capstone seam, is not applied here)

platform.elf_flags: 0x30005, RVC, double-float ABI, cheriabi, capability mode -- asserted by build.sh, not assumed
platform.qemu: qemu-system-riscv64xcheri 7.1.0 from the SDK; no -cpu sstc=false, which this QEMU has no property for
platform.guest: CheriBSD purecap, cheribsd-riscv64-purecap.img; motd reports INVARIANTS WITNESS CHERI_CAPREVOKE
platform.disk: a qcow2 overlay over OUR OWN copy of the image: the shared one is held open by a peer lane's guest and an overlay over it fails to take even a shared write lock
platform.transfer: virtio-9p (kldload virtio_p9fs; mount -t p9fs -o trans=virtio phpcorpus /mnt/php)

result.php -n -v: PHP 5.0.0 (cli) banner printed, rc=1 -- native PHP 5.0.0 exits 1 for -v as well
result.reading: the interpreter starts, compiles and executes under purecap, and its sort path survives. That is the gate the Perl purecap port did not pass (SIGPROT inside perl_construct on every invocation), so this port CAN host a corpus arm
